title: Binary and Ternary Neural Networks: A Survey of Learning and Acceleration
content: Binary and ternary neural networks reduce the number of values used to represent weights or activations, creating opportunities for compact models and inexpensive computation. Their development now spans image recognition, language understanding, generative models, and large language model (LLM) inference, with implementations ranging from commodity processors to specialized memory and logic. This survey brings these directions together around three coupled questions: how discrete models acquire and preserve useful capabilities, how their representations are encoded and executed, and which deployment conditions make them preferable to wider alternatives. We review optimization and architecture design, native low-bit pretraining, conversion of pretrained models, activation and state quantization, and acceleration on CPUs, GPUs, FPGAs, ASICs, and emerging computing substrates. Within-study comparisons illustrate why training and calibration choices can matter as much as nominal precision, and why a compact format may favor either lookup or wider matrix arithmetic. The synthesis identifies recurring trade-offs among representational capacity, learning cost, data movement, and hardware flexibility. In particular, ternary sparsity is useful only when its structure matches execution, while cheaper projections increase the importance of attention, persistent state, and the surrounding runtime. We conclude with research directions for capability-preserving quantization, executable model formats, and workload-aware co-design.
